title: SailPoint Admin Domain 3 questions (3.1 identity profiles, 3.2 attribute mappings, 3.3 lifecycle states)
note: Original questions written for Delzar Certification Academy. Not from exam dumps or commercial banks; not affiliated with SailPoint.

questions.stem: An administrator creates an identity profile and selects the Workday source in it. What does this do to the Workday source?
choices: It becomes a target source that receives identity attributes through attribute sync
It is moved from its virtual appliance connection to a direct cloud connection
It is scheduled for a nightly delta aggregation in place of full aggregations
It becomes authoritative, and an identity is created for each account
questions.answer: It becomes authoritative, and an identity is created for each account
questions.explanation: Linking a source to an identity profile makes it authoritative, so its accounts become identities. Attribute sync to targets is a separate provisioning feature and is not what an identity profile turns on.

questions.stem: A new administrator asks which group of settings is configured on an identity profile rather than on a source. Which answer is BEST?
choices: Connection credentials, aggregation schedules and the account correlation settings
Access request approvers, certification reviewers and campaign reminder emails
Virtual appliance clusters, network proxy settings and connector log levels
Sign-in and security settings, identity attribute mappings and lifecycle states
questions.answer: Sign-in and security settings, identity attribute mappings and lifecycle states
questions.explanation: An identity profile holds the security (authentication) settings, the identity attribute mappings and the lifecycle states for its identities. Credentials, schedules and correlation are configured on the source itself.

questions.stem: A company connects its HR system as a source and aggregates it, but no identity profile has been created yet. What is the result of the aggregation?
choices: Accounts are aggregated, but no identities are created from them
An identity is created for every account using the default mappings
The aggregation fails until an identity profile is linked to the source
Each account becomes an identity in a disabled lifecycle state
questions.answer: Accounts are aggregated, but no identities are created from them
questions.explanation: Identities are created only from authoritative sources, and a source becomes authoritative through an identity profile. Aggregation itself still works, so it does not fail.

questions.stem: An administrator deletes an identity profile that is no longer needed. What happens to the source that the profile was built on?
choices: The source and all of its aggregated accounts are deleted
The source's accounts are deprovisioned on the target system
The source remains but is no longer authoritative
The source is converted into a delimited file source
questions.answer: The source remains but is no longer authoritative
questions.explanation: Deleting an identity profile does not delete its source or deprovision accounts; it only makes the source non-authoritative. The profile's identities are deleted unless they can move to another profile.

questions.stem: Before deleting an identity profile, what must an administrator confirm about the identities in it?
choices: That all of them are currently in an active lifecycle state
That each one has completed a recent manager certification
That none of them are source owners or application owners
That their accounts have been exported to a CSV report first
questions.answer: That none of them are source owners or application owners
questions.explanation: An identity profile cannot be deleted while its identities still own sources or apps, so those ownerships must be moved first. Lifecycle state and certification status do not block the deletion.

questions.stem: An identity profile is deleted, and its identities cannot be reassigned to any other identity profile. What happens to those identities' source accounts?
choices: They become uncorrelated accounts
They are disabled on every connected source
They move to a default catch-all identity profile
They are deleted from the tenant and the target systems
questions.answer: They become uncorrelated accounts
questions.explanation: When identities are deleted with their profile, their source accounts remain but become uncorrelated. Deleting a profile never deprovisions or disables target accounts.

questions.stem: An administrator tries to create a new identity profile, but the tenant will not allow it at that moment. Which condition is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The source has no entitlements aggregated yet
Another profile already uses the same description
An account aggregation is currently running
The tenant has no custom identity attributes defined
questions.answer: An account aggregation is currently running
questions.explanation: Identity profiles cannot be created or deleted while an account aggregation is running. Entitlements, descriptions and custom attributes are not prerequisites for creating a profile.

questions.stem: Which statement about identity profiles and identities is accurate?
choices: An identity merges the mappings of every profile whose source it matches
An identity profile can point to several authoritative sources at once
Each identity is associated with only one identity profile at a time
Identity profiles apply only to identities that hold an admin user level
questions.answer: Each identity is associated with only one identity profile at a time
questions.explanation: An identity can belong to only one identity profile, and each profile is built on one authoritative source. That is why priority matters when a person exists on several authoritative sources.

questions.stem: Employees come from an HR system and contractors from a separate vendor-management system. The two groups need different mappings and lifecycle rules. What is the BEST design?
choices: Create a single identity profile and add both sources to it as authoritative
Create two identity profiles on the HR source and filter contractors into one
Create one identity profile per authoritative source and set priority
Mark the contractor source as authoritative on the source's own settings page
questions.answer: Create one identity profile per authoritative source and set priority
questions.explanation: Each identity profile is built on one authoritative source, so two populations from two systems get two profiles, ordered by priority. A source is made authoritative by an identity profile, not by a source setting.

questions.stem: Three identity profiles were created in this order: Employees, Contractors, Partners. No one has changed their priority. Which profile has the highest priority?
choices: Partners, because the most recently created profile gets the highest priority
Contractors, because priority is assigned by alphabetical order of the names
None of them, because all profiles share equal priority until it is changed
Employees, because the earliest profile created gets the highest priority
questions.answer: Employees, because the earliest profile created gets the highest priority
questions.explanation: By default identity profiles are prioritized by creation order, so the first one created is highest. Priority is not alphabetical and is never left equal.

questions.stem: By default, which priority value does the first identity profile created in a tenant receive?
choices: A value of 10, which is the highest priority
A value of 1, which is the lowest priority
A value of 100, which is the highest priority
A value of 20, which is the lowest priority
questions.answer: A value of 10, which is the highest priority
questions.explanation: The first identity profile gets priority 10 and is the highest; the next gets 20, and so on. A lower number therefore means a higher priority.

questions.stem: Identities that exist in both the HR and contractor sources should be governed by the Contractors profile, which was created second. How can the administrator change the order?
choices: Rename the Contractors profile so that it sorts first in the list
Update the profiles' priority values with the Update Identity Profile API
Raise the contractor source's account deletion threshold above HR's
Schedule the contractor source to aggregate before the HR source
questions.answer: Update the profiles' priority values with the Update Identity Profile API
questions.explanation: Identity profile priority is changed by updating each profile's priority attribute through the API. Names, deletion thresholds and aggregation timing do not affect which profile wins.

questions.stem: Why does the priority of identity profiles matter in a tenant with several authoritative sources?
choices: It sets the order in which the authoritative sources' scheduled aggregations are started
It controls which profile's lifecycle states are reviewed first in certification campaigns
It decides which profile's administrators can approve access requests for its identities
It decides which profile an identity joins when it is on several authoritative sources
questions.answer: It decides which profile an identity joins when it is on several authoritative sources
questions.explanation: An identity is associated with the highest-priority profile where it has an authoritative account. Priority does not order aggregations, certifications or approvals.

questions.stem: A person's account is removed from the HR source, which backs the highest-priority profile. They still have an account on the contractor source, which backs another profile. What is MOST likely to happen to the identity?
choices: It is reassigned to the contractor profile, where it has an authoritative account
It is deleted at once, because its first authoritative account is gone
It stays in the HR profile with its last known attribute values forever
It becomes an uncorrelated account on the contractor source instead
questions.answer: It is reassigned to the contractor profile, where it has an authoritative account
questions.explanation: Identities are associated with the highest-priority profile where they still have an authoritative account, so the identity can move to the contractor profile. It is only deleted when no authoritative account remains.

questions.stem: An organization is choosing which of its systems to make authoritative. Which source is the BEST choice?
choices: The ticketing system, which holds requests from some users
The HR system, which holds a complete record of every worker
A file share group list, which holds the members of one project
The visitor badge system, which holds only on-site guests
questions.answer: The HR system, which holds a complete record of every worker
questions.explanation: An authoritative source should provide a complete list of the people to be governed, which is usually HR or a directory. Partial lists would create incomplete or missing identities.

questions.stem: After an acquisition, an administrator creates a third identity profile for the acquired company's HR feed. Some acquired staff also appear in the main HR feed. Without changes, which profile will those staff be associated with?
choices: The new acquisition profile, because newer profiles take precedence
Whichever profile's source was aggregated most recently for them
The main HR profile, because it was created earlier and ranks higher
Both profiles, with attributes merged from the two HR feeds
questions.answer: The main HR profile, because it was created earlier and ranks higher
questions.explanation: Older profiles have higher priority by default, so people on both feeds join the main HR profile. An identity never belongs to two profiles at once.

questions.stem: Where does an administrator go to view the priority, processing status and identity exception reports for each authoritative source configuration?
choices: Admin > Connections > Sources > Account Schema
Admin > Global > Security Settings > Password
Admin > Identity Management > Identity Profiles
Admin > Search > Saved Searches > Subscriptions
questions.answer: Admin > Identity Management > Identity Profiles
questions.explanation: The Identity Profiles list shows each profile's priority, status and any identity exceptions. The other pages hold source schemas, global security and search features.

questions.stem: Which identity profile sign-in method lets users authenticate with the password of their account on a selected source?
choices: Directory Connection
Site User Name and Password
Multifactor Authentication
Untrusted Geography
questions.answer: Directory Connection
questions.explanation: Directory Connection checks the user's password against the chosen authentication source, which is pass-through authentication. The site user name and password option uses a password created at registration.

questions.stem: A profile uses the tenant's own User Name and Password sign-in method. What do users in that profile sign in with?
choices: The user name and password they created when they registered
Their Active Directory password checked through a virtual appliance
A one-time code that is emailed to their manager at each sign-in
A client ID and secret generated from a personal access token
questions.answer: The user name and password they created when they registered
questions.explanation: With the site user name and password method, users sign in with the credentials they set up during registration. Checking an AD password through a VA is the Directory Connection method.

questions.stem: Security wants every user in the Contractors identity profile to sign in using a mobile authenticator app such as Duo Mobile. Which identity profile setting meets this?
choices: Enable Two-Factor Authentication in the password reset and unlock settings
Select Mask Phone Numbers in the password reset settings
Select Multifactor Authentication in the Sign-in Method settings
Select Untrusted Geography under the Block Access From settings
questions.answer: Select Multifactor Authentication in the Sign-in Method settings
questions.explanation: The Multifactor Authentication sign-in option requires a mobile authenticator to sign in. Two-Factor Authentication in the reset settings only applies to password resets and unlocks.

questions.stem: An administrator turns off the Multifactor Authentication option on an identity profile that contains several org admins. How does this affect the admins' sign-in?
choices: The admins sign in with a password only, like other users
The admins are still required to use MFA to sign in
The admins lose access until the option is turned back on
The admins must switch to pass-through authentication
questions.answer: The admins are still required to use MFA to sign in
questions.explanation: Admins are always required to use MFA even if the checkbox is disabled on their identity profile. Disabling it changes sign-in only for non-admin users in that profile.

questions.stem: Which section of an identity profile holds the choice between the site user name and password, Directory Connection and Multifactor Authentication?
choices: Sign-in Method
Password Reset and User Unlock Methods
Block Access From
Invitation Options
questions.answer: Sign-in Method
questions.explanation: Sign-in Method is where the authentication options are chosen. Password reset methods control how users reset or unlock, and Block Access From restricts where they can sign in from.

questions.stem: A help desk lead asks why some users in the tenant sign in with their AD password while others use a password they created at registration. What is the MOST likely explanation?
choices: The users belong to identity profiles that use different sign-in methods
The users have been assigned different user levels in the tenant
The users were aggregated through two different virtual appliance clusters
The users have lifecycle states with different technical names
questions.answer: The users belong to identity profiles that use different sign-in methods
questions.explanation: The sign-in method is set per identity profile, so users in different profiles can authenticate differently. User levels control admin rights, not the sign-in method.

questions.stem: Which situation is the BEST reason to choose the site user name and password sign-in method for an identity profile?
choices: The profile's users all need to sign in with their existing AD passwords
The profile's users have no directory account that pass-through could check
The tenant must avoid sending any registration invitations to these users
The profile's authoritative source is connected through a virtual appliance
questions.answer: The profile's users have no directory account that pass-through could check
questions.explanation: Users without a directory account cannot use pass-through authentication, so a tenant password set at registration fits them. Users who sign in with AD passwords need Directory Connection instead.

questions.stem: What is pass-through authentication in Identity Security Cloud?
choices: Accepting a signed SAML assertion that an external IdP has issued
Forwarding a user's access request to the source owner for an approval
Copying each source password into the tenant's own credential store
Signing in with a network password that is verified against a source
questions.answer: Signing in with a network password that is verified against a source
questions.explanation: Pass-through authentication lets users sign in with the password of their account on a source such as Active Directory. Accepting an IdP's SAML assertion is single sign-on, a different option.

questions.stem: An administrator wants users in one population to use their Active Directory passwords when they sign in to the tenant. Where is this configured?
choices: Global security settings, in the service provider configuration
Sign-in Method on the identity profile, set to Directory Connection
The AD source's create account provisioning policy
The access profile that grants the AD entitlements
questions.answer: Sign-in Method on the identity profile, set to Directory Connection
questions.explanation: Pass-through authentication is chosen per identity profile by selecting Directory Connection and an authentication source. Service provider settings are for SAML single sign-on.

questions.stem: Several identities show the status Authentication Source Mismatch. Their identity profile uses Directory Connection with Active Directory as the authentication source. What is the cause?
choices: Their AD passwords have expired since the last aggregation
Those identities have no correlated account on the AD source
Their lifecycle state values do not match the technical name case
Their AD accounts are correlated to more than one identity each
questions.answer: Those identities have no correlated account on the AD source
questions.explanation: Authentication Source Mismatch means the identity has no account on the source used for pass-through, so it cannot authenticate. Expired passwords would cause a sign-in failure, not this identity status.

questions.stem: An identity shows Authentication Source Mismatch, and the person really does have an AD account. Which action resolves the status?
choices: Run a delta aggregation of the authoritative source
Reset the identity's password in the tenant
Assign the identity the Helpdesk user level
Correlate the person's AD account to the identity
questions.answer: Correlate the person's AD account to the identity
questions.explanation: The fix is to correlate an account on the authentication source to the identity, or to change the profile's sign-in method. Aggregating the authoritative source or resetting a tenant password does not link the AD account.

questions.stem: Pass-through authentication against an on-premises Active Directory depends on which component to reach the directory?
choices: The virtual appliance that connects the AD source
A personal access token issued to each user
A SAML trust between AD and the tenant
An event trigger subscribed to sign-in events
questions.answer: The virtual appliance that connects the AD source
questions.explanation: On-premises sources such as AD are reached through the virtual appliance, which also carries pass-through authentication requests. A SAML trust is used for SSO with an IdP, not for checking AD passwords.

questions.stem: What is the main benefit of pass-through authentication for end users?
choices: They never need any password, because the source vouches for them silently
They are exempt from multifactor prompts for every administrative action
They receive access to every source account as soon as they sign in
They reuse their existing network password instead of a new tenant one
questions.answer: They reuse their existing network password instead of a new tenant one
questions.explanation: Pass-through authentication means users sign in with the network password they already know. It does not remove passwords, skip admin MFA or grant access.

questions.stem: Which pair of settings must be chosen together on an identity profile to set up pass-through authentication?
choices: Multifactor Authentication and Mask Phone Numbers
Invitation Options and Off Network blocking
Directory Connection and an Authentication Source
Two-Factor Authentication and an email template
questions.answer: Directory Connection and an Authentication Source
questions.explanation: Pass-through needs the Directory Connection sign-in method plus the source whose password is checked. The other pairs control MFA, phone masking, invitations and network blocking.

questions.stem: A profile is switching to Directory Connection with AD as the authentication source, but some of its contractors have no AD account. What is the BEST way to keep the contractors able to sign in?
choices: Give the contractors the Helpdesk user level so they can bypass the directory
Keep the contractors in a separate profile that uses the site user name and password
Enable Mask Phone Numbers on the profile so contractors can reset by text
Map the contractors' Last Name attribute from AD so they correlate to it
questions.answer: Keep the contractors in a separate profile that uses the site user name and password
questions.explanation: Identities without an account on the authentication source cannot use pass-through and would show Authentication Source Mismatch. A separate profile with a tenant password suits users with no directory account.

questions.stem: An administrator selects Block Access From Off Network on an identity profile but has not defined any network block. What happens?
choices: The setting has no effect until a network block is defined
All users in that profile are blocked from signing in
Only users outside the organization's home country are blocked
Only admins in that profile are blocked from signing in
questions.answer: All users in that profile are blocked from signing in
questions.explanation: If Off Network is selected with no network definition, every user in the profile is blocked. Admins must define the allowed network block before enabling the option.

questions.stem: Compliance requires that users in one identity profile cannot sign in from countries on the organization's untrusted list. Which setting applies?
choices: Block Access From Off Network
Password reset Mask Phone Numbers
Enable Two-Factor Authentication
Block Access From Untrusted Geography
questions.answer: Block Access From Untrusted Geography
questions.explanation: Untrusted Geography blocks sign-in from countries on the configured block list, or outside the trusted list. Off Network blocks by IP address range instead of by country.

questions.stem: Security wants users to pass two verification methods before they can reset their tenant password or unlock their account. Which identity profile setting does this?
choices: Choose Multifactor Authentication as the profile's sign-in method
Enable Two-Factor Authentication in the password reset and unlock settings
Select Untrusted Geography in the Block Access From settings
Require manager approval for resets in the profile's access request settings
questions.answer: Enable Two-Factor Authentication in the password reset and unlock settings
questions.explanation: Two-Factor Authentication in the reset settings requires two of the enabled reset and unlock methods. The Multifactor Authentication sign-in method affects normal sign-in, not resets.

questions.stem: Which identity profile option hides most of the digits of a user's contact number while they reset their password?
choices: Mask Phone Numbers
Enable Two-Factor Authentication
Block Access From Off Network
Directory Connection
questions.answer: Mask Phone Numbers
questions.explanation: Mask Phone Numbers turns on phone number masking during password resets. Two-Factor Authentication changes how many methods are needed, not what is shown.

questions.stem: New hires are created in a pre-hire lifecycle state two weeks before they start. HR wants them invited to the tenant only on their first day. What should the administrator configure?
choices: Manual invitations sent each week from the HR source's list of new accounts
A certification campaign that reviews identities in the pre-hire state
An access profile in the pre-hire state that contains an invitation
Automatic invitations for identities that enter the active lifecycle state
questions.answer: Automatic invitations for identities that enter the active lifecycle state
questions.explanation: With provisioning enabled, an identity profile can send invitations automatically when identities enter a chosen lifecycle state. Pre-hire to active on the start date is the typical example.

questions.stem: What does the Password Reset and User Unlock Methods section of an identity profile control?
choices: Which source account passwords are changed when a user resets the tenant password
How often users in the profile must change their tenant password to stay active
Which verification options users have to reset a password or unlock an account
Which administrators may unlock users in the profile from the Identities page
questions.answer: Which verification options users have to reset a password or unlock an account
questions.explanation: This section lists the verification methods available for resetting the tenant password or unlocking the account. Password expiry and source password sync are separate password settings.

questions.stem: Users in a profile that uses the site user name and password have never signed in. Neither pass-through authentication nor SSO is configured. What must happen before they can sign in?
choices: They must be assigned an active lifecycle state
They must be invited and complete registration
Their manager must certify their current access
Their HR account must be aggregated a second time
questions.answer: They must be invited and complete registration
questions.explanation: Without an external option such as pass-through or SSO, only invited users can sign in, and registration is where they set their password. A lifecycle state alone does not create sign-in credentials.

questions.stem: An administrator is making a new HR source authoritative. Put the steps in order.
items: Go to Admin > Identity Management > Identity Profiles and select Create New
Enter a name and description and choose the HR source
Configure the sign-in method, password reset options and access blocks
Save the profile and open its Mappings page to map identity attributes
Preview a few identities, then select Apply Changes
questions.explanation: The profile is created on the source, its security settings are set and saved, then mappings are defined. Preview checks the values before Apply Changes processes the identities.

questions.stem: Match each identity profile setting to its effect.

pairs.match: Checks the user's password against a chosen source
Requires a mobile authenticator app at sign-in
Requires two methods to reset a password or unlock
Blocks sign-in from outside the defined IP ranges
Blocks sign-in from countries on the block list

targets_extra: Requires manager approval for each sign-in
questions.explanation: Sign-in method options decide how users authenticate, Two-Factor Authentication applies to resets and unlocks, and the Block Access From options restrict where sign-in is allowed. There is no manager approval of sign-ins.

questions.stem: An architect is documenting what an identity profile determines for its identities. Which TWO items belong on the list?
choices: The identity attribute mappings that populate identity data
The access granted or removed as lifecycle states change
The schedule for aggregating entitlements from the source
The virtual appliance cluster used by the source
The approval scheme for requesting the source's roles
answers: The identity attribute mappings that populate identity data
The access granted or removed as lifecycle states change
questions.explanation: An identity profile sets authentication settings, attribute mappings and lifecycle-state access. Aggregation schedules and VA clusters belong to the source, and approval schemes belong to access items.

questions.stem: Which identity attributes must be mapped in every identity profile and cannot be null for any identity?
choices: First Name, Department and Manager
Display Name, Title and Location
User Name, Work Email and Last Name
Lifecycle State, Start Date and End Date
questions.answer: User Name, Work Email and Last Name
questions.explanation: User Name (uid), Work Email (email) and Last Name (lastname) are the required identity attributes. Missing values generate identity exceptions; the others are optional.

questions.stem: Two identities from different identity profiles resolve to the same User Name value. How does the tenant respond?
choices: It merges the two identities into a single identity record
It appends a sequence number to the second identity's User Name
It keeps both, because uniqueness applies only within a profile
It generates an identity exception for the duplicate User Name
questions.answer: It generates an identity exception for the duplicate User Name
questions.explanation: User Name must be unique across all identities from every identity profile, and a duplicate raises an identity exception. The tenant does not merge identities or rename them.

questions.stem: An HR record has a malformed work email value with no at sign. The Work Email mapping copies the value unchanged. What happens?
choices: An identity exception is raised, because the email is not a valid address
It is accepted, because Work Email is not validated as an address
The identity is created with an empty Work Email and flagged as incomplete
The mapping falls back to the identity's personal email address instead
questions.answer: It is accepted, because Work Email is not validated as an address
questions.explanation: Work Email cannot be null, but it is not validated as an email address. The admin should fix the data in HR rather than expect the tenant to reject it.

questions.stem: Identity exceptions appear on the HR identity profile after aggregation. What is the recommended way to resolve them?
choices: Delete the affected identities and create them again by hand on the Identities page
Change the profile's sign-in method so the missing values are no longer required
Download the exception report, fix the source data and aggregate again
Raise the source's account deletion threshold so that the exceptions are ignored
questions.answer: Download the exception report, fix the source data and aggregate again
questions.explanation: Identity exceptions mean accounts are missing required attributes or have a duplicate User Name. The report shows which values are missing so they can be corrected at the source and re-aggregated.

questions.stem: Access requests and certifications in the tenant need to route work to each identity's manager. What must the administrator set up?
choices: Add each manager as a source owner of the authoritative source
Create a custom identity attribute named manager and leave it unmapped
Map Manager Name and define manager correlation on the source
Map the Manager Name attribute with the E.164 Phone Format transform
questions.answer: Map Manager Name and define manager correlation on the source
questions.explanation: Manager features need the Manager Name attribute mapped and manager correlation logic defined for the source. Source ownership is unrelated to who an identity's manager is.

questions.stem: An identity appears as Incomplete on the Identities page. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: It is missing a value for a required identity attribute
It has no access profiles or roles assigned yet
It has not signed in to the tenant since it was created
It has accounts on more than one connected source
questions.answer: It is missing a value for a required identity attribute
questions.explanation: Identities missing required attributes are shown as Incomplete and also produce identity exceptions. Having no access or not signing in does not make an identity incomplete.

questions.stem: Before an identity profile can automatically grant birthright access and disable leavers' accounts based on employment status, which identity attribute must be mapped?
choices: Identification Number (identificationNumber)
Lifecycle State (cloudLifecycleState)
License Status (licenseStatus)
Next Processing (nextProcessing)
questions.answer: Lifecycle State (cloudLifecycleState)
questions.explanation: Lifecycle-state provisioning only works when the Lifecycle State attribute is mapped for the profile. The other default attributes do not assign lifecycle states.

questions.stem: The Employees identity profile is built on the HR source, but the work email address exists only in Active Directory. How should Work Email be mapped?
choices: Make AD the profile's authoritative source instead of HR
Add AD to the profile as a second authoritative source
Copy the email into HR by hand before mapping the attribute
Map Work Email from the mail attribute on the AD source
questions.answer: Map Work Email from the mail attribute on the AD source
questions.explanation: Identity attributes can be mapped from account attributes on any source, not only the authoritative one. A profile has a single authoritative source, so adding AD as a second one is not possible.

questions.stem: Which statement about where identity attribute values can come from is accurate?
choices: They can be mapped only from the profile's authoritative source
They can be mapped from account attributes on any source
They can be mapped only from sources on the same virtual appliance
They can be mapped only from flat file sources loaded by an admin
questions.answer: They can be mapped from account attributes on any source
questions.explanation: Mappings may use any source's account attributes, so a profile can combine HR data with AD email, for example. The source connection type does not restrict mappings.

questions.stem: An administrator no longer wants the Title attribute populated for one identity profile. How is the mapping removed?
choices: Set the Source dropdown for Title to None
Delete the Title attribute from all profiles
Set the Transform dropdown for Title to ToLower
Remove the title column from the source schema
questions.answer: Set the Source dropdown for Title to None
questions.explanation: Choosing None in the Source dropdown unmaps the attribute for that profile. Title is a default attribute that should not be deleted, and changing the schema could break other mappings.

questions.stem: Employees' department should come from HR, while contractors' department should come from AD. Each group has its own identity profile. How is this handled?
choices: Map the department attribute differently in each identity profile
Create two department attributes, one for each of the two source systems
Use a role to copy department values between the two groups
Make the AD source authoritative for the department attribute
questions.answer: Map the department attribute differently in each identity profile
questions.explanation: The list of identity attributes is shared, but each identity profile has its own mappings. That lets the same attribute come from different sources for different populations.

questions.stem: When an administrator maps an identity attribute directly to an account attribute, which two dropdowns are selected on the Mappings page?
choices: Transform and Rule
Profile and Priority
Source and Attribute
Schema and Connector
questions.answer: Source and Attribute
questions.explanation: A direct mapping is a source plus one of its account attributes. A transform or rule is only added when the value must be changed or calculated.

questions.stem: The source attribute mapped to User Name contains values such as j.smith(contractor). What risk does this create?
choices: Users may be unable to sign in, because the value has disallowed characters
Identity processing converts those characters to underscores automatically
The tenant rejects every aggregation of that source until the data is fixed
Attribute sync stops updating the source accounts for those identities
questions.answer: Users may be unable to sign in, because the value has disallowed characters
questions.explanation: Characters such as asterisk, parentheses, ampersand, exclamation mark and period must not be in the source attribute mapped to a sign-in attribute. Users with such values may not be able to sign in.

questions.stem: Which part of identity data can differ between two identity profiles in the same tenant?
choices: The list of identity attribute names that are available
The technical names of the custom attributes
The set of attributes that are always required
The mappings that populate each identity attribute
questions.answer: The mappings that populate each identity attribute
questions.explanation: Attribute names, technical names and the required set are shared by every profile, but each profile maps them its own way. A custom attribute added in one profile appears in all of them.

questions.stem: International users must be able to receive password reset codes by text message. Which built-in transform must be applied to the mapping of their work number?
choices: ISO3166 Country Format
ToUpper
E.164 Phone Format
Remove Diacritical Marks
questions.answer: E.164 Phone Format
questions.explanation: The E.164 Phone Format transform must be applied to Work Phone for international numbers. ISO3166 converts country names, not phone numbers.

questions.stem: Values such as United States arrive from HR as full names, but a downstream system needs two-letter codes such as US. Which built-in transform fits?
choices: E.164 Phone Format
RFC5646
User Preferred Name
ISO3166 Country Format
questions.answer: ISO3166 Country Format
questions.explanation: ISO3166 Country Format converts a country name to its two-character code. RFC5646 produces language tags, which look similar but serve a different purpose.

questions.stem: Last names arrive with accented characters that an older target system cannot store. Which built-in transform helps?
choices: ToLower
ISO3166 Country Format
E.164 Phone Format
Remove Diacritical Marks
questions.answer: Remove Diacritical Marks
questions.explanation: Remove Diacritical Marks converts accented letters to their base characters. ToLower changes case only and leaves the accents in place.

questions.stem: What must happen before a custom rule can be used to calculate an identity attribute?
choices: The rule must be uploaded to every virtual appliance in the cluster
The rule must be saved as a static transform in the Admin UI first
The rule must be approved by the source owner of the mapped source
SailPoint must review the rule before it is deployed to the tenant
questions.answer: SailPoint must review the rule before it is deployed to the tenant
questions.explanation: Unlike transforms, rules must be reviewed by SailPoint before they can be implemented. Transforms can be created and uploaded by the tenant's own administrators.

questions.stem: How does an administrator select an approved rule for an identity attribute mapping?
choices: Choose Complex Data Source as the source, then choose the rule
Choose the authoritative source, then type the rule name as the attribute
Choose None as the source, then upload the rule file to the mapping
Choose any source, then select the rule in the Attribute dropdown
questions.answer: Choose Complex Data Source as the source, then choose the rule
questions.explanation: Rules are picked by setting Source to Complex Data Source and selecting the rule in the Transform dropdown. Choosing None unmaps the attribute.

questions.stem: A team wants to change how one identity attribute is calculated without waiting for an external review. Which approach is BEST?
choices: Use a rule, because rules are deployed instantly by the tenant admins
Use a role, because roles can rewrite identity attribute values
Use a workflow, because workflows replace identity mappings
Use a transform, because transforms do not need a SailPoint review
questions.answer: Use a transform, because transforms do not need a SailPoint review
questions.explanation: Transforms are configuration the tenant can create and apply, while rules need SailPoint review. Roles and workflows do not calculate identity attribute mappings.

questions.stem: An identity's lifecycle state should be worked out from its start date and end date. Which mapping approach does SailPoint describe for this?
choices: A simple ToUpper transform applied to the start date attribute
A custom attribute for each date, with the Source set to None
The User Preferred Name transform applied to the end date
A complex transform that combines several operations
questions.answer: A complex transform that combines several operations
questions.explanation: Simple transforms can be combined into complex transforms, for example to calculate a lifecycle state from a start date. A single case-changing transform cannot compare dates.

questions.stem: A source attribute holds several values, and an administrator applies a mapping transform to it. What will the identity attribute contain?
choices: All values joined into one comma-separated string
Only the first value, as a single value
All values kept as a multi-valued identity attribute
No value, because transforms reject multi-valued data
questions.answer: Only the first value, as a single value
questions.explanation: A mapping transform on a multi-value attribute takes only the first value and returns a single value. Admins should not expect the other values to be kept.

questions.stem: An administrator adds a custom identity attribute while editing the Employees identity profile. Where does the new attribute appear?
choices: Only in the Employees profile, until it is copied to the others
In every profile, though it need not be mapped in each one
Only in profiles whose source schema has a matching column
In every profile, and it must be mapped in all of them
questions.answer: In every profile, though it need not be mapped in each one
questions.explanation: Any attribute added under one identity profile appears in all profiles, but each profile can leave it unmapped. Only the required attributes must be mapped everywhere.

questions.stem: An administrator enters Hire Date as the name of a new identity attribute. Which technical name is generated automatically?
choices: hireDate
hire_date
hire-date
Hire Date
questions.answer: hireDate
questions.explanation: The technical name is a camel case version of the name, so Hire Date becomes hireDate. The name field accepts only letters, numbers and spaces.

questions.stem: Which characters does the Name field accept when an administrator adds a new identity attribute?
choices: Letters, numbers and underscores
Letters, periods and hyphens
Any printable characters
Letters, numbers and spaces
questions.answer: Letters, numbers and spaces
questions.explanation: The Name field accepts only letters, numbers and spaces, and the camel case technical name is generated from it. Underscores and punctuation are not accepted.

questions.stem: An administrator deletes a custom identity attribute while editing the Contractors identity profile. What is the scope of the deletion?
choices: The attribute is deleted from all identity profiles
The attribute is deleted only from the Contractors profile
The attribute is hidden but keeps its values on identities
The attribute is deleted only where it was never mapped
questions.answer: The attribute is deleted from all identity profiles
questions.explanation: Deleting a custom attribute in one profile deletes it from every profile. Admins should check every place it is used before saving the deletion.

questions.stem: An administrator plans to delete a custom identity attribute. Which dependency is MOST important to check first?
choices: Roles whose membership criteria use the attribute
The connector log level set on the virtual appliance
The account aggregation schedule of the source
The branding colors used in email templates
questions.answer: Roles whose membership criteria use the attribute
questions.explanation: Deleting an attribute can break role membership criteria, sign-in user name settings, SAML maps, rules, transforms and lifecycle calculations that use it. Log levels and branding are unaffected.

questions.stem: A custom identity attribute has just been deleted. Which follow-up processing does SailPoint require?
choices: Run a full account aggregation on every source connected to the tenant
Run identity processing on each profile, even where it was unmapped
Run a certification campaign on every identity that held the attribute
Restart every virtual appliance so the old attribute leaves its cache
questions.answer: Run identity processing on each profile, even where it was unmapped
questions.explanation: Identity processing must be run on each identity profile after deleting a custom attribute, even where it was not mapped. Aggregations, campaigns and VA restarts do not clear it.

questions.stem: On the Mappings page, an administrator selects Remove on a custom attribute and then selects Cancel at the warning message. What happens?
choices: The attribute is deleted anyway, but all of the other unsaved changes are kept
The attribute is restored, and all other unsaved changes are reverted too
The attribute is restored, and other unsaved changes are kept
The attribute is hidden until the administrator saves the page
questions.answer: The attribute is restored, and all other unsaved changes are reverted too
questions.explanation: Cancel at the warning restores the attribute to the list but also reverts every other unsaved change. Admins should save other work before removing attributes.

questions.stem: The administrator team wants to delete the default costCenter identity attribute because it is unused. What is the recommended action?
choices: Delete it with Remove and then Save on the Mappings page of any profile
Delete it only after unmapping it in every identity profile first
Leave it in place, because default attributes should not be deleted
Rename it as a custom attribute and then delete the custom copy
questions.answer: Leave it in place, because default attributes should not be deleted
questions.explanation: Default identity attributes should not be deleted; SailPoint Support should be contacted if needed. An unused default attribute can simply be left unmapped.

questions.stem: After an administrator saves new mappings, the identity profile shows the status Needs Processing. What should the administrator do to update its identities?
choices: Select Apply Changes for that identity profile
Run a delta aggregation of an unrelated source
Delete the profile and create it again
Wait for the next certification campaign
questions.answer: Select Apply Changes for that identity profile
questions.explanation: Saved mapping changes are applied to identities when the admin selects Apply Changes, which starts identity processing. Re-creating the profile would delete its identities.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the Preview feature on an identity profile's Mappings page?
choices: To show which accounts will be deleted during the next account aggregation
To check how the mappings populate a chosen identity's attributes before applying
To send a sample lifecycle state change email to all of the profile's administrators
To compare the profile's mappings with those in a configuration hub backup
questions.answer: To check how the mappings populate a chosen identity's attributes before applying
questions.explanation: Preview lets the admin select an identity and see the attribute values the mappings produce. It is a verification step before Apply Changes.

questions.stem: A new Department mapping has been saved but not applied. What is true about existing identities in the profile?
choices: Their attributes were recalculated at the moment the mapping was saved
Their attributes have not yet been recalculated with the new mapping
Their attributes were cleared and stay empty until Apply Changes
Their attributes are locked and cannot change from aggregation
questions.answer: Their attributes have not yet been recalculated with the new mapping
questions.explanation: Saving changes marks the profile as Needs Processing; identities are updated when changes are applied or processing runs. Existing values are not cleared in the meantime.

questions.stem: Which two statuses can an identity profile show on the Identity Profiles list?
choices: Enabled or Disabled
Draft or Published
Active or Needs Processing
Healthy or Unhealthy
questions.answer: Active or Needs Processing
questions.explanation: Identity profiles are Active or Needs Processing, the latter after changes that have not been applied. Healthy and Unhealthy are used for things such as virtual appliances and sources.

questions.stem: HR changes a person's department, and the HR source is aggregated as scheduled. What updates the identity's department attribute without any administrator action?
choices: A certification campaign that the aggregation launches for the identity
An access request that the aggregation raises on the identity's behalf
Identity processing that runs automatically after the aggregation
A configuration hub restore that the aggregation schedules overnight
questions.answer: Identity processing that runs automatically after the aggregation
questions.explanation: Identity data changed by aggregation is processed automatically, which recalculates the mapped attributes. Certifications and requests do not update identity attributes.

questions.stem: An identity profile is marked as having scheduled processing. What is the reason?
choices: A mapping uses a transform or rule that is tagged to need a periodic refresh
The profile's authoritative source has a delta aggregation scheduled every day
The profile's lifecycle states send a notification email every morning
The profile was created during an account aggregation of its source
questions.answer: A mapping uses a transform or rule that is tagged to need a periodic refresh
questions.explanation: Scheduled processing is shown when a mapped rule or transform is tagged for periodic refresh, such as date-based calculations that change without new source data. Aggregation schedules are a source setting.

questions.stem: An administrator is changing the Department mapping for a profile with 20,000 identities and wants to limit risk. What should be done FIRST after saving the change?
choices: Apply the changes at once so all identities are updated together
Delete the old Department attribute so the new one can be added
Preview several identities to confirm the new values are correct
Disable the profile's lifecycle states until the change is done
questions.answer: Preview several identities to confirm the new values are correct
questions.explanation: Preview verifies the mapping on real data before Apply Changes processes every identity. Applying first risks pushing wrong values to thousands of identities and any roles or syncs that use them.

questions.stem: An administrator is adding a new Hire Date identity attribute fed from HR. Put the steps in order.
items: Select Add New Attribute on the Mappings page and enter the name
Select the HR source and its hire date account attribute
Choose a transform if the date needs to be reformatted
Preview an identity to verify the value
questions.explanation: The attribute is added and mapped, with an optional transform, then saved. Preview checks the result before Apply Changes processes the identities.

questions.stem: Match each built-in mapping transform to what it does.

pairs.match: Converts a phone number into the international standard format
Converts a country name into a two-character code
Converts accented letters to their base characters
Converts the value to lowercase letters
Builds the display name from the preferred name when it exists

targets_extra: Converts a date into the tenant's time zone
questions.explanation: These are built-in simple transforms selectable on the Mappings page. Date conversion is done with a dateFormat transform, which is not one of these options.

questions.stem: An administrator is building a new identity profile. Which TWO identity attributes must be mapped before identities are created without exceptions?
choices: User Name (uid)
Work Email (email)
Department (department)
Manager Name (manager)
Start Date (startDate)
questions.explanation: User Name, Work Email and Last Name are required for every identity. Department, manager and start date are useful but optional.

questions.stem: Which lifecycle states are included automatically when an administrator creates a new identity profile?
choices: Joiner, mover and leaver, plus a disabled state
Enabled, disabled and deleted, plus a pending state
Requested, approved and provisioned, plus a failed or expired state
Pre-hire, active, leave of absence, terminated and archived
questions.answer: Pre-hire, active, leave of absence, terminated and archived
questions.explanation: New identity profiles include pre-hire, active, leave of absence, terminated and archived states. Joiner, mover and leaver are the business events these states support, not state names.

questions.stem: An administrator created a Retired lifecycle state and mapped retirees' HR status to its technical name, but no identities are assigned to it. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The lifecycle state has no email notification list
The lifecycle state has not been enabled
The lifecycle state has no access profiles to grant
The lifecycle state has no description entered
questions.answer: The lifecycle state has not been enabled
questions.explanation: Lifecycle states are disabled by default and must be enabled before identities are assigned to them. Notifications and access profiles are optional.

questions.stem: Where are lifecycle states defined in Identity Security Cloud?
choices: Once for the tenant, under the global settings
In each source, under the account schema
Separately in each identity profile
In each role, under the membership criteria
questions.answer: Separately in each identity profile
questions.explanation: Lifecycle states are configured per identity profile, so employees and contractors can have different states and access. They are not global, per source or per role.

questions.stem: New hires should automatically receive email, VPN and intranet access on their first day. Which configuration BEST fits?
choices: A certification campaign that reviews each new hire's access
An access request that each new hire submits on the first day
An active lifecycle state that grants the needed access profiles
A search subscription that emails the help desk about each new hire
questions.answer: An active lifecycle state that grants the needed access profiles
questions.explanation: Lifecycle states drive joiner access automatically by granting access profiles when the identity enters the state. Requests and campaigns need people to act and are not automatic birthright access.

questions.stem: When a worker leaves, all of their source accounts should be switched off automatically. Which feature handles this?
choices: An identity profile priority change for leavers
A source account deletion threshold set to zero
A terminated lifecycle state configured to disable accounts
A manager certification launched on the end date
questions.answer: A terminated lifecycle state configured to disable accounts
questions.explanation: A lifecycle state can enable, disable or delete source accounts when an identity enters it, which automates leaver processing. The deletion threshold only protects against mass deletions during aggregation.

questions.stem: Staff on extended leave should keep their accounts but lose VPN access until they return. The active state grants VPN through an access profile. What is the BEST configuration?
choices: A leave of absence state that deletes the VPN account on all sources
A terminated state that is assigned to staff while they are on leave
An archived state that removes all access for staff while on leave
A leave of absence state that does not grant the VPN access profile
questions.answer: A leave of absence state that does not grant the VPN access profile
questions.explanation: Access profiles granted by one state are revoked when the identity moves to a state that does not grant them, so the VPN access is removed while other accounts remain. Terminated and archived would remove far more access.

questions.stem: How many lifecycle states can one identity be assigned at the same time?
choices: Exactly one lifecycle state at a time
One lifecycle state for each source account
One lifecycle state for each assigned role
Up to two while a mover change is pending
questions.answer: Exactly one lifecycle state at a time
questions.explanation: An identity has one lifecycle state at a time, set by its cloudLifecycleState value or manually. States are not per account or per role.

questions.stem: An administrator wants the lifecycle states of an identity profile to appear in a specific order in the Lifecycle Management panel. How is the display order changed?
choices: Rename the states so that they sort in alphabetical order
Change the identity profile's priority value in the list
Disable and re-enable the states in the wanted order
Update each state's priority value through the API
questions.answer: Update each state's priority value through the API
questions.explanation: The display order of lifecycle states is set by their priority attribute, updated through the lifecycle state API. Identity profile priority is a different setting that decides profile membership.

questions.stem: An identity moves from the active state to leave of absence. What happens to the access profiles that the active state granted?
choices: They stay assigned until the next certification campaign removes them
They stay assigned, because lifecycle access is granted only once
They are revoked unless the leave of absence state also grants them
They are moved into a pending access request for the manager
questions.answer: They are revoked unless the leave of absence state also grants them
questions.explanation: Access profiles granted by a lifecycle state are revoked when the identity leaves the state, unless the new state also grants them. No certification or request is involved.

questions.stem: An administrator removes an access profile from an identity that is still in the lifecycle state that grants it. What happens next?
choices: It is provisioned again, because the state enforces it
The access stays removed until the identity changes state
The access is removed and the lifecycle state is disabled
The access stays removed and an exception is logged
questions.answer: It is provisioned again, because the state enforces it
questions.explanation: Access profiles assigned through a lifecycle state are enforced while the identity remains in that state, so removed access is provisioned again. To remove it for good, change the state's configuration.

questions.stem: The terminated state has Remove all access enabled, but security wants terminated users to keep one mailbox entitlement for 30 days. What is the BEST approach?
choices: Turn off Remove all access and remove the other access by hand instead
Grant an access profile with the mailbox entitlement in the terminated state
Add the mailbox source to the terminated state's Delete Accounts list
Mark the mailbox entitlement as requestable so that it is skipped by removal
questions.answer: Grant an access profile with the mailbox entitlement in the terminated state
questions.explanation: Access profiles listed in a state's Access Profiles tab are excluded from Remove all access. Wrapping the entitlement in an access profile keeps it while everything else is removed.

questions.stem: An identity has two accounts on one source, and its lifecycle state grants an access profile on that source. Which account receives the access?
choices: The one chosen by the access profile's multiple account options
The account that was created most recently on the source system
The account that was correlated first to the identity
Both accounts, because lifecycle access is per account
questions.answer: The one chosen by the access profile's multiple account options
questions.explanation: When an identity has several accounts on a source, the access profile's multiple account options decide which account gets the access. Creation or correlation order is not used.

questions.stem: Which tab of a lifecycle state is used to grant birthright access to the identities in that state?
choices: Settings for Previous Accounts
Email Notification List
Identity State
Access Profiles
questions.answer: Access Profiles
questions.explanation: The Access Profiles tab lists the access profiles granted to identities in the state. Settings for Previous Accounts enables, disables or deletes accounts instead.

questions.stem: The terminated state disables accounts on all sources but also grants an access profile on the mailbox source. What happens to a terminated user's mailbox account?
choices: It is disabled first and then the access profile is granted to it again
It is not disabled, because the state grants an access profile on that source
It is deleted, because a granted access profile overrides the disable setting
It is disabled, and the access profile is removed at the same time
questions.answer: It is not disabled, because the state grants an access profile on that source
questions.explanation: Source accounts are not disabled or deleted when the source has an access profile listed in the state's Access Profiles tab. This keeps the granted access usable.

questions.stem: When are identities' lifecycle states and the matching provisioning actions recalculated?
choices: Only when an admin runs a certification campaign on the identity
Only when the virtual appliance is restarted
Only when a user signs in to the tenant
During event-driven and scheduled identity processing
questions.answer: During event-driven and scheduled identity processing
questions.explanation: Lifecycle state changes and their provisioning are worked out during identity processing, which runs after aggregation and on a schedule. Sign-in and campaigns do not trigger it.

questions.stem: Which type of access item can a lifecycle state grant directly to identities?
choices: Roles
Applications
Access profiles
Individual entitlements
questions.answer: Access profiles
questions.explanation: Lifecycle states grant access profiles; a single entitlement is granted by putting it in an access profile. Roles are assigned through their own membership criteria, which can use the cloudLifecycleState attribute.

questions.topic: Account Actions and Remove All Access
questions.stem: The terminated state has Remove all access turned on. Which access does a terminated identity keep?
choices: Access from birthright roles and access profiles granted by the current state
Access that was requested within the last 30 days and approved by their manager
Access on sources whose accounts are set to be disabled rather than deleted
Access that was certified as approved in the most recent campaign
questions.answer: Access from birthright roles and access profiles granted by the current state
questions.explanation: Remove all access keeps items provisioned from birthright roles and the access profiles granted by the current state. Recent requests and certification decisions are removed.

questions.topic: Account Actions and Remove All Access
questions.stem: Removing an entitlement normally needs approval. What happens when the Remove all access setting of a lifecycle state removes it?
choices: The removal waits for the source owner
The removal waits for the manager
The removal is skipped for that item
The removal approval is bypassed
questions.answer: The removal approval is bypassed
questions.explanation: When Remove all access removes an access item that needs removal approval, the approval is automatically bypassed. Leaver access is removed without waiting for approvers.

questions.topic: Account Actions and Remove All Access
questions.stem: An administrator cannot configure the Delete Accounts option on a lifecycle state even with Specific sources chosen. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: The state does not have Remove all access turned on yet
The state does not send email to all SailPoint admins
The state is still marked as the profile's default state
The state's identity state is not set to Inactive (long-term)
questions.answer: The state's identity state is not set to Inactive (long-term)
questions.explanation: Delete operations can only be configured when the lifecycle state's identity state is Inactive (long-term). Delete is also unavailable when All sources is selected.

questions.topic: Account Actions and Remove All Access
questions.stem: A lifecycle state disables accounts on All sources. A new source is connected to the tenant next month. Is it included?
choices: No, the state must be edited to add the new source
Yes, newly created sources are included automatically
No, All sources covers only sources that existed at save
Yes, but only after the source's first certification
questions.answer: Yes, newly created sources are included automatically
questions.explanation: When All sources is selected, newly created sources are included automatically. Sources can be left out with the Excluded Sources list.

questions.topic: Account Actions and Remove All Access
questions.stem: Accounts on every source except HR should be disabled when an identity enters the terminated state. What is the BEST configuration?
choices: Choose No sources for Disable Accounts and turn on Remove all access
Choose All sources for Delete Accounts and then add HR to Excluded Sources
Choose All sources for Disable Accounts and add HR to Excluded Sources
Choose Specific sources and add HR to the Disable Accounts list
questions.answer: Choose All sources for Disable Accounts and add HR to Excluded Sources
questions.explanation: All sources with an exclusion disables everything except HR and also covers future sources. Adding HR to Specific sources would do the opposite, and Delete is not available with All sources.

questions.topic: Account Actions and Remove All Access
questions.stem: An administrator wants the terminated state to both disable and delete Active Directory accounts. What will the tenant allow?
choices: Both operations, run in the order disable first and then delete
Both operations, but only when All sources is selected for each
Only one operation for AD, because a source gets one per state
Neither operation, because AD accounts cannot be disabled by states
questions.answer: Only one operation for AD, because a source gets one per state
questions.explanation: A source cannot be configured for multiple operations in the same lifecycle state. The admin chooses either disable or delete for AD in that state.

questions.topic: Account Actions and Remove All Access
questions.stem: Accounts deleted by the archived lifecycle state are recreated on the next identity refresh. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The identity still has a role with entitlements on that source
The archived state still sends email to the identity's manager
The identity profile priority is lower than another profile's
The source's account deletion threshold blocked the deletion
questions.answer: The identity still has a role with entitlements on that source
questions.explanation: If an assigned role includes entitlements on the source, the account is recreated because the role is still in force. SailPoint recommends removing such roles before deleting accounts.

questions.topic: Account Actions and Remove All Access
questions.stem: Which out-of-the-box lifecycle states have Remove all access turned on by default?
choices: Pre-hire and active
Terminated and archived
Active and leave of absence
Leave of absence and terminated
questions.answer: Terminated and archived
questions.explanation: Remove all access is enabled by default for the out-of-the-box terminated and archived states. Leave of absence keeps access unless an admin changes it.

questions.topic: Account Actions and Remove All Access
questions.stem: A lifecycle state's disable action fails with a retryable error from the target system. How does the tenant handle it?
choices: It retries the request once per hour, up to three times
It retries the request every few minutes until it succeeds
It never retries and closes the request as failed
It retries once a day until the next certification
questions.answer: It retries the request once per hour, up to three times
questions.explanation: Lifecycle state provisioning that fails with a retryable error is retried once per hour, up to three times. Persistent failures then need admin attention.

questions.topic: Account Actions and Remove All Access
questions.stem: After an identity entered the terminated state and its accounts were disabled, someone re-enabled one account directly on the target. Will the lifecycle state disable it again automatically?
choices: Yes, the next identity refresh disables the account again every time
Yes, but only when the source owner approves the repeated action
No, because the re-enabled account is deleted from the tenant
No, lifecycle account actions run once and are not re-enforced
questions.answer: No, lifecycle account actions run once and are not re-enforced
questions.explanation: Enable and disable actions of a lifecycle state execute a single time and are not a persistent retry or enforcement mechanism. Unlike lifecycle-granted access profiles, account status is not re-enforced.

questions.stem: What determines which lifecycle state an identity is assigned to automatically?
choices: The value of its cloudLifecycleState identity attribute
The value of the lifecycle state's priority attribute in the API
The order in which the identity's source accounts were aggregated
The user level that is assigned to the identity in the tenant
questions.answer: The value of its cloudLifecycleState identity attribute
questions.explanation: Each identity's cloudLifecycleState attribute value selects the lifecycle state with the matching technical name. The state priority only sets display order.

questions.stem: HR sends the value Active, but the lifecycle state's technical name is active. What happens to the identity?
choices: It is not assigned the state and shows a technical name case mismatch
It is assigned the active state, because the match ignores letter case
It is assigned the first enabled lifecycle state in the identity profile
It is moved to another identity profile that has an Active state
questions.answer: It is not assigned the state and shows a technical name case mismatch
questions.explanation: The match between the attribute value and the technical name is case-sensitive, so Active does not assign active. The identity shows Lifecycle State Does Not Match Technical Name Case.

questions.stem: HR's status field holds single-letter codes such as A, L and T, while the lifecycle states are active, leaveOfAbsence and terminated. What is the BEST way to assign the states?
choices: Apply a transform to the cloudLifecycleState mapping to convert each code
Rename the lifecycle states so that their display names are A, L and T on the profile
Set each identity's lifecycle state by hand after every aggregation of the HR source
Map the attribute from HR without changes and let the tenant guess the closest name
questions.answer: Apply a transform to the cloudLifecycleState mapping to convert each code
questions.explanation: A transform can normalize source values into the exact technical names that cloudLifecycleState needs. Manual assignment is reset when the source value changes and does not scale.

questions.stem: An identity shows the status Lifecycle State Not Set. What does this mean?
choices: The value does not match any of the lifecycle states defined for the identity's profile
The attribute is not mapped for the profile or its value is null for the identity
The value matches a lifecycle state, but that state has not yet been enabled
The value matches a lifecycle state, but with different upper and lower case
questions.answer: The attribute is not mapped for the profile or its value is null for the identity
questions.explanation: Not Set means the Lifecycle State attribute is unmapped or null. A value that matches no state is Not Valid, and a case difference has its own status.

questions.stem: An identity shows the status Lifecycle State Not Valid. What is the cause?
choices: The attribute is not mapped in the identity profile, so the value is always empty
The identity was set to a lifecycle state manually by an administrator
The value matches none of the lifecycle states in the identity's profile
The attribute value is correct, but provisioning to a source failed
questions.answer: The value matches none of the lifecycle states in the identity's profile
questions.explanation: Not Valid means a value exists but does not correspond to any lifecycle state in that identity profile. Each profile has its own set of states.

questions.stem: An administrator manually sets an identity's lifecycle state to inactive. Later, HR changes the person's status value on the source. What happens to the lifecycle state?
choices: It stays inactive until an administrator changes it again
It stays inactive, and the new HR value raises an exception
It resets to the state calculated from the new source value
It switches to the profile's first enabled lifecycle state
questions.answer: It resets to the state calculated from the new source value
questions.explanation: A manual setting holds only while the underlying source value is unchanged; when the value changes, the state is recalculated automatically. The UI then shows the state as Automatic.

questions.stem: On an identity's details page, how can an administrator tell that its lifecycle state was set by hand rather than calculated?
choices: The state name is shown in red on the identity page
The state name is followed by Manual in parentheses
The identity is flagged with an identity exception
The identity's profile shows Needs Processing
questions.answer: The state name is followed by Manual in parentheses
questions.explanation: Lifecycle states changed through a manual action display (Manual), while calculated ones show (Automatic). No exception or profile status is raised.

questions.stem: Where does an administrator confirm the exact technical name that the cloudLifecycleState value must match?
choices: In parentheses next to the state name at the top of the lifecycle state page
In the source's account schema, beside the HR status column
In the email template that is used for lifecycle state change messages
In the identity profile's priority column on the profiles list
questions.answer: In parentheses next to the state name at the top of the lifecycle state page
questions.explanation: The technical name appears in parentheses next to the lifecycle state name on its page. The cloudLifecycleState value must match it exactly, including case.

questions.stem: The lifecycle state calculation needs logic too complex for transforms. What does SailPoint recommend?
choices: A second identity profile that holds the complex logic
A manual lifecycle state change made for every identity every day by an admin
A certification that sets the state for each reviewer
A custom rule built with SailPoint Professional Services or a partner
questions.answer: A custom rule built with SailPoint Professional Services or a partner
questions.explanation: For logic beyond transforms, SailPoint suggests a custom rule built by Professional Services or an implementation partner. Rules go through SailPoint review.

questions.stem: A role should be assigned automatically only to identities whose lifecycle state is active. What is the BEST way to configure the role?
choices: Add the role to the active lifecycle state's Access Profiles tab so it is granted
Request the role for each active identity by hand
Use membership criteria where the cloudLifecycleState attribute equals active
Set the role's owner to the identity profile's owner
questions.answer: Use membership criteria where the cloudLifecycleState attribute equals active
questions.explanation: Role membership criteria can use identity attributes, including cloudLifecycleState. Lifecycle states grant access profiles, not roles, in their Access Profiles tab.

questions.stem: Which identity state must an identity have to be selected in the Request Center?
choices: Inactive (short-term)
Inactive (long-term)
Active
Any identity state
questions.answer: Active
questions.explanation: Only Active identities can be selected in the Request Center or the My Team list. Inactive identities are limited in which services they appear in.

questions.stem: Separated workers should drop out of most services, with one final attribute sync when they change state. Which identity state should their lifecycle state use?
choices: Inactive (short-term)
Inactive (long-term)
Active
No identity state
questions.answer: Inactive (long-term)
questions.explanation: Inactive (long-term) is for identities who have left; a final attribute sync runs on entry and they no longer appear in most services. Short-term is for leave or separation in progress.

questions.stem: Workers on parental leave should stay in scheduled identity processing for role and access profile changes but are not fully active. Which identity state fits BEST?
choices: Inactive (long-term)
Active
Archived
Inactive (short-term)
questions.answer: Inactive (short-term)
questions.explanation: Inactive (short-term) suits people on leave or separating; scheduled and manual processing still applies. Archived is a lifecycle state, not an identity state.

questions.stem: A lifecycle state has no identity state configured. Which identity state do identities in that lifecycle state receive?
choices: Inactive (short-term)
Active
Inactive (long-term)
Null, so they are skipped
questions.answer: Active
questions.explanation: If the assigned lifecycle state has no configured identity state, or the identity has no lifecycle state, the identity state is set to Active automatically.

questions.stem: HR wants the person's manager and a shared HR mailbox told whenever someone enters the terminated state. Which lifecycle state setting is used?
choices: Settings for Previous Accounts, with All sources selected
